jobs.title: Senior Data Protection Specialist
jobs.descriptionText:
August 2026
Job description
749185328_1 1 www.mills-reeve.com
Data Protection Specialist
Risk and Compliance, permanent, full time
The role
This is an exciting opportunity to join the General Counsel function at Mills & Reeve. Reporting to the General
Counsel, this role is responsible for developing and taking ownership of key aspects of the firm's operational and
commercial data protection programme.
The Data Protection Specialist will be a trusted adviser to partners, lawyers and business services teams, helping the
firm navigate complex data protection requirements in a pragmatic and commercially focused way. The role combines
technical expertise with practical problem-solving and relationship management, working closely with stakeholders
across the business to ensure data protection is effectively embedded into decision-making, procurement, technology,
supplier management and client engagements.
You will take ownership of significant areas of the firm's data protection programme, with particular responsibility for
supplier management, client and supplier contractual requirements, data protection due diligence, international data
transfer governance, auditing and wider regulatory compliance activities. You will help ensure that data protection is
effectively embedded into business processes, commercial decision-making and risk management activities. You will
take ownership of key workstreams, driving activity forward, identifying improvements and implementing practical, riskbased solutions that support the firm's strategic and operational objectives.
This role can be based in any of our regional offices.
The activities
Shared data protection advice and response activity
• Responding to data incidents (immediate response; drafting ICO notification; drafting data subject notifications;
identifying clients to be notified).
• Responding to regulatory queries.
• Responding to complaints with data aspects.
• Responding to data subject rights requests as a third-line support with support from the Senior Regulatory &
Compliance Solicitor and the Senior Data Protection Specialist.
• Responding to queries from Marketing, particularly around lawful marketing practices and use of personal data
and consent, providing pragmatic, risk-based advice supporting business objectives. 
749185328_1 2 www.mills-reeve.com
• Supporting the People team in responding to employee rights requests, including subject access requests,
rectification and erasure requests, reviewing disclosures and advising on exemptions where appropriate.
• Providing expert data protection advice to support the firm's investigation function, including advising on the lawful
handling, sharing and disclosure of personal data in internal investigations, and ensuring compliance with UK
GDPR principles including proportionality, data minimisation, confidentiality and appropriate access controls.
• Receiving and responding to ad hoc fee earner and partner queries.
Supplier management
• Reviewing and negotiating data protection provisions in supplier and third-party contracts.
• Reviewing supplier and third-party responses to data protection questions during the procurement process.
• Checking supplier and third-party sub-processors for issues.
• Receiving and responding to notifications from suppliers about changes to sub-processors.
• Receiving and responding to supplier notifications of data incidents.
Client-side contracts
• Taking responsibility for data protection content in letters of engagement and terms and conditions.
• Reviewing bespoke client contracts and terms.
• Maintaining records of data protection clauses with clients, including notification obligations and timescales and
liaising with colleagues on AI-related contractual provisions where relevant.
• Responding to bids and tenders and liaising with colleagues on AI-related elements where required.
• Supporting compliance with the annual NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit completion.
Internal auditing and reporting
• Conducting or procuring appropriate data protection auditing activity and working with the data protection team
and other departments to implement resulting corrections.
• Supporting and contributing to other internal and external assurance frameworks.
• Reviewing and maintaining data protection content within the firm's risk register, identifying and escalating key
data protection risks.
• Supplying data protection content for ISO annual management reporting.
• Conducting root cause and statistical analysis regarding data incidents and developing and implementing
corrective actions.
Internal departmental support
• Providing pragmatic, risk-based data protection advice to Marketing, the People team, investigations teams, fee
earners and Partners. 
749185328_1 3 www.mills-reeve.com
• Supporting employee rights request responses, including reviewing disclosures and advising on exemptions
where appropriate.
• Providing data protection input into internal investigations to support lawful handling, sharing and disclosure of
personal data.
Governance records
• Maintaining awareness of governance records activity and supporting the Senior Data Protection Specialist where
necessary.
Culture and awareness
• Supporting the Senior Data Protection Specialist in promoting a strong data protection culture across the firm.
The person
The role would suit an experienced data protection professional with a strong background in operational and
commercial data protection, ideally gained within a law firm, professional services business or similarly regulated
environment.
You will combine strong technical knowledge with sound commercial judgement. You will have the confidence to apply
your knowledge in a pragmatic, risk-based way. You will enjoy working independently, taking ownership of significant
areas of responsibility and driving matters through to completion.
You will have experience operating within a complex organisation where data moves across multiple systems, teams,
processes and third-party providers. You will be comfortable understanding and analysing complex data flows and
advising on the practical implications of business, technology and procurement decisions. You have a focus on noncontentious data protection (contracts, supplier management, international data transfers), and can assist with
responding to, and advising a range of internal stakeholders on, data subject rights, incidents, supplier and client-side
data protection requirements, and broader governance obligations.
Given the responsibilities of this role, it is likely that your background and experience will include:
• strong knowledge of UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 and related regulatory guidance, with the ability to
translate legal and regulatory requirements into practical business advice for senior stakeholders.
• significant experience of non-contentious data protection work, including contracts, supplier management,
procurement processes, data protection impact assessments and governance activities.
• strong commercial awareness and the ability to balance regulatory requirements, business objectives and risk
considerations.
• confidence operating independently and confident in setting and prioritising multiple competing demands.
• effective self-management and confidence in setting and prioritising their own work agenda.
• excellent written and verbal communication skills, able to convey complex matters clearly to different
audiences.
• confidence in building sustainable relationships with clients, partners, lawyers and business services
colleagues.
• a structured, organised and methodical approach.
• a proactive mindset with a genuine interest in developing operational processes and improving how data
protection is delivered across the firm.
The role additionally requires someone who:
• works collaboratively and contributes positively to a supportive team culture;
749185328_1 4 www.mills-reeve.com
• is curious, pragmatic and confident in exercising judgement;
• is self-managing, organised and able to prioritise effectively when faced with competing demands;
• has strong attention to detail whilst maintaining a focus on broader commercial and strategic objectives; and
• has a genuine interest in improving processes, governance arrangements and the way data protection is
delivered across the firm.
The package
As you’d expect, we offer a competitive salary and a wide range of benefits. You can find out more about our core
staff benefits here.
Pre-employment screening
If we make you an offer for a role, we will conduct a range of pre-employment screening. This will include, but is not
limited to, a basic DBS check, right to work check, address verification, any disciplinary history recorded with the
Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) and a self-declaration to assess your character and suitability for the role. Full
details of our screening process are available on request.
Our business services career structure
Here at Mills & Reeve our business services career structure has five levels and a clear progression framework. This
role fits within the manager level of our framework, and the job description includes the types of activities expected for
this type of role. If you’d like more information on our career structure, our HR team will be happy to provide further
details.
The firm
At Mills & Reeve, our 1,450 plus people and over 850 lawyers share one vision – achieve more together. It’s a state of
mind in every client relationship we start and every choice we make. And it’s what clients consistently say
distinguishes us from your average law firm.
You can expect a close and attentive working relationship with a team that’s responsive when you need them. You’ll
receive advice tailored to your individual needs. Wherever in the world you or your business needs support, we’ll draw
on our network to give recommendations.
We’re driven by our values – we’re ambitious, we’re open, we care and we collaborate. We embrace new ideas,
communicate honestly and are easy to work with. We’re committed to you, our planet, our communities and each
other.
We’ve been listed in The Sunday Times Best Places to Work list as one of the best big organisations, and we’ve
recently been reaccredited Platinum Investors in People status – a standard achieved by only 8% of assessed
organisations.
Don’t just take our word for it though. Have a read through our People Perspectives to find out more about some of
our team and their experiences at Mills & Reeve.
749185328_1 5 www.mills-reeve.com
And finally
Everyone at Mills & Reeve brings a unique perspective and ideas to the team and we do everything we can to help
each person to thrive. We’re committed to providing an inclusive and supportive working environment, are happy to
consider flexible working arrangements, and want to achieve the right balance for both our people and the firm. We
encourage everyone to ask if they feel they need any workplace adjustments, and will do our best to support with
these.
Promoting equality and diversity across our firm is a key pillar of our strategy, and our five staff networks are an
integral part of this. To find out more about our diversity and inclusion work, visit our webpage here.
Want to find out more?
If you’d like any more information about Mills & Reeve take a look at our website.

jobs.title: Senior Manager Rider Onboarding and Compliance
jobs.descriptionText:
About the job
Our Global Structure

Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation and growth drives everything we do.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager to join our Rider Onboarding and Compliance team. The team sits at the heart of the Rider Support Centre (RSC) and are responsible for getting new applicants out on the road quickly and safely, and for keeping active riders compliant once they're there. It's a centralised, all-markets function, and it has a direct line to two things Deliveroo cares about most: rider retention and rider satisfaction.

What You’ll Be Doing

Your number one goal: Deliver the right rider hours, in the right areas, with compliant riders.

Reporting into the Head of Rider Services, you'll lead the Rider Onboarding & Compliance team comprising; 3 Team Leads circa 30+ in-house Representatives split across our London and Manchester offices, circa 30+ person team in Deliveroo India In addition you'll hold a couple of outsource vendor partners accountable for performance; delivering business-as-usual onboarding and compliance support across every Deliveroo market. You'll own the strategy, run the large global projects that come with it, and act as the applicant and rider advocate across the business, not just the person accountable for the KPIs.

Here’s What Your Day-to-day Might Look Like

Deliver core marketplace operational metrics: Own and execute the global rider onboarding and compliance strategy to ensure we deliver the right rider hours, in the right areas, with fully compliant riders.
Lead distributed global teams: Lead, coach, and scale a multi-layered operational team across the UK, an in-house team of 30+ in India, and external BPO vendor partners.
Drive large-scale strategic initiatives: Plan and execute major projects, including onboarding pipeline standardisation and compliance process redesigns in close collaboration with Legal, Policy, and Data Science. Manage vendor performance and capacity: Direct outsource vendor productivity and set up robust forecasting and capacity models to effectively manage end-to-end team resourcing and global volume shifts.
Advocate for riders and continuous improvement: Act as the primary rider advocate across the business to resolve complex escalations, leverage new tooling or automation, and drive operational excellence.

What You’ll Need to Thrive

Our Ideal Candidate Will Bring Expertise In

Proven operational leadership: Significant experience leading multi-layered, multi-site teams in a fast-paced environment (such as onboarding, trust & safety, compliance, or customer support operations).
Vendor & BPO management expertise: Hands-on capability in managing external outsource vendor partners, holding them accountable to strict quality and compliance standards while building collaborative, outcome-focused relationships.
Resource and capacity planning: Strong commercial and analytical skills with demonstrated ability to build forecasting models and optimise headcount across internal and offshore resources.
Cross-functional stakeholder management: Proven ability to partner with Legal, Policy, and Data Science teams to navigate complex regulatory, risk, and fraud requirements without sacrificing speed or rider experience.
Change management and execution: A strong bias to action with a track record of implementing process changes, automation, and tooling that lift efficiency across distributed teams.

Why Join Us?

At Deliveroo, customer care is central to how we build trust across our marketplace. You’ll work in a fast-paced, global environment where service excellence drives real impact.

🔧 Make a visible impact every day Your work directly improves outcomes for customers, riders and restaurant partners.

🌱 Grow through ownership Take responsibility for complex cases and help shape improvements to how we operate.

🧠 Develop deep operational expertise Work across teams and markets to build strong regulatory and service knowledge.

🌎 Deliver together in an inclusive culture Collaborative, values-driven teams that support how you work best. We aim to create a fair process that lets your skills shine — our interview typically includes 3–4 stages. Learn more about how we hire here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!

Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness.

jobs.title: Client Data Manager
jobs.descriptionText:
Role Overview

The Pioneer Programme has established a global, three-divisional client data platform that contributes to the ultimate client experience for CHANEL, enabling international client recognition. Bringing together 200+ internal and external stakeholders across Business, IT, Legal, Regions and Divisions, it fosters cross-functional collaboration around a shared client-centric vision.

As part of the Global PMO, you will lead key global client data management initiatives, partnering with Business, IT, Legal, Security, Data Governance and external partners to drive scalable, compliant and client-focused solutions. You will play a central role in shaping data governance, data quality, privacy and client data capabilities while ensuring alignment across a complex global organisation.

This role requires strong expertise in client data management, stakeholder engagement, governance and project delivery within an international matrix environment.

Reports to: Head of Global PMO – Pioneer

Key Responsibilities

Client Data Management & Governance


Act as the primary point of contact for Business stakeholders on all client data management topics.
Define, maintain and continuously improve client data management frameworks, including client matching and merging rules, calculated fields, business rules and data quality controls.
Drive initiatives to improve data quality, completeness, consistency and accuracy across client data platforms, within Regions and Divisions.
Lead the development, governance and evolution of the client data model, ensuring alignment with business requirements and enterprise data standards.
Support the definition and implementation of data governance principles, roles, responsibilities and core client data management processes.
Act as Global Data Steward, driving best practices, governance standards and data ownership across Regions and Divisions.
Facilitate and animate the global Data Steward community through training, guidance, documentation and knowledge-sharing activities.


Data Privacy & Compliance


Lead the design, harmonisation and continuous improvement of global client data privacy processes, including Data Subject Rights to Access, Modification and Erasure, as well as the implementation of the Global Client Data Retention Policy.
Partner with Legal, Security and Regional teams to ensure compliance with applicable privacy regulations and internal governance requirements.
Support the development of scalable and automated privacy solutions across markets.


Analytics 


Support the enhancement of client analytics capabilities through the evolutions of calculated fields, KPI definitions and reporting requirements.
Establish and maintain client data quality monitoring frameworks and dashboards, coordinating cross-functional analysis, remediation and preventive actions to improve data accuracy, completeness and consistency.


Programme & Stakeholder Management


Coordinate complex, cross-functional client data initiatives involving business, technical and external stakeholders.
Lead stakeholder discussions to gather requirements, assess impacts, identify risks and propose pragmatic solutions.
Support the preparation of governance materials, executive presentations, roadmaps, guidelines and decision-making documentation for steering committees and leadership forums.
Monitor progress, risks, dependencies and action plans across multiple projects and regions.


Documentation & Knowledge Management


Own and maintain client data documentation, governance practices, process flows, business rules and operational processes.
Manage and continuously update the central knowledge repository (WikiPioneer/SharePoint), ensuring documentation remains accurate, accessible and up to date.
Support change management and training initiatives through the creation of user guides, standards and communication materials.


Team Leadership


Provide day-to-day guidance, coaching and prioritisation support to the Client Data Coordinator and the Global Data Steward Intern
Foster collaboration, team engagement and strong cross-functional relationships across the Pioneer community.


Required Experience


Significant experience in client data management, data governance, data quality or master data management initiatives.
Hands-on experience with client data analytics, KPI development, reporting and data quality analysis, combined with a strong analytical mindset and the ability to translate data into insights.
Strong knowledge of CRM, customer data platforms and client journeys.
Experience managing complex cross-functional projects and transformation programmes in an international environment.
Proven ability to work across Business, IT, Legal, Security and external partner organisations.
Experience defining business requirements, operating models, governance frameworks and process improvements.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations and client data lifecycle management.
Experience with client data platforms, data stewardship practices and analytics solutions is highly desirable.


Key Skills & Competencies


Client Data Management & Governance
Data Stewardship & Data Quality Management
Master Data Management (MDM)
CRM & Customer Experience
Client Data Analytics & Insights
Analytical Thinking & Data-Driven Decision Making
Data Privacy & Compliance
Business Analysis & Requirements Management
Project & Programme Management
Stakeholder Management & Influencing
Change Management & Training
Risk & Incident Management
Process Design & Continuous Improvement
Communication & Executive Presentation Skills


What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be customer-focused, collaborative and highly effective at navigating complex stakeholder environments. They will combine analytical thinking with strong communication skills, be comfortable operating with ambiguity, and demonstrate the ability to influence, align and drive outcomes across a global matrix organisation.

They will thrive on solving complex problems, building collaborative relationships, and delivering sustainable, scalable solutions that strengthen CHANEL's client data capabilities worldwide.

jobs.descriptionText:
About the job
Company Description

Publicis Re:Sources is at the core of Publicis Groupe, the world's largest communications company. We are the only full-service, end-to-end shared service organisation in the industry, enabling Groupe agencies to do what they do best: innovate and transform for their clients.

Formed in 1998 as a small team to service a few Publicis Groupe firms, Publicis Re:Sources has grown to 6,000+ employees in over 55 countries. We provide technology solutions and business services, including finance, accounting, legal, benefits, procurement, tax, real estate, treasury and risk management, information security, and global mobility — supporting 110,000+ employees across the Publicis Groupe network. Our people are at the centre of everything we do, bringing curiosity, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence to their work every day.

Learn more about Publicis Re:Sources and the Publicis Groupe agencies we support at publicisresources.com



Overview

Publicis is seeking an experienced, self-motivated, flexible Data Privacy Lawyer to assist our business in the UK. This is a full-time position in London. You will be a member of our Global Data Privacy Office (GDPO) and report to a senior member of the GDPO. The role is broad and involves advising across our business on the various privacy risks, obligations and other issues related to privacy. We are looking for someone who has demonstrated excellent legal and privacy judgment alongside strategic thinking. We would also like someone who is diligent, proactive, practical and fun to work with.

This role will be based in our London office. Please only apply if you have the right to work in the UK.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

 Key point of contact for data privacy-related enquiries for some of our advertising, creative, technology, data and health agencies in the UK.
 Support internal teams, providing them with appropriate advice and guidance, with the ability to effectively collaborate and communicate with diverse cross-functional teams.
 Provide support to members of the commercial and employment legal teams on privacy matters and serve as subject matter expert on all privacy issues impacting or relating to the business and employees across the Groupe.
 Collaborate with our Global Data Privacy Operations team to adapt data governance materials such as inventory templates, vendor due diligence questionnaires, proprietary system questionnaires, and privacy impact assessment questionnaires.
 Assist the commercial legal team in drafting, reviewing and negotiating data privacy provisions in complex commercial contracts.
 Maintain current knowledge of all relevant privacy legislation and regulations and distribute this knowledge across both the legal function and the wider business.
 Provide data protection and privacy advice relating to data partnerships and vendor relationships, and assist in drafting, reviewing and negotiating data privacy provisions in related contracts.
 Help develop data privacy training materials and conduct privacy training.

Qualifications

Requirements:

 Qualified UK solicitor. Common law jurisdiction equivalent lawyers will also be considered.
 Privacy certification (such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US from IAPP or similar) is desirable.
 5+ years of legal experience, ideally within privacy but commercial and privacy combined experience will also be considered.
 Flexible working with a minimum of three days a week in the London office.
 In-house legal experience is desirable, particularly AdTech or technology experience with knowledge of digital advertising, including providing digital advertising/media counseling and transactional support to digital media companies, publishers, social media marketing, or online platforms in the AdTech/data space (e.g. ad serving, programmatic, data management, measurement, and analytics).
 Direct experience applying UK and European privacy laws, regulations, and industry guidelines, especially those relevant for media and advertising.
 Commercially minded with good communication and inter-personal skills to enable the individual to work with all levels of internal management and negotiate with external clients.
 Enthusiastic, energetic data protection and privacy subject matter expert, with good knowledge of the latest regulatory changes and the related impacts on the media and advertising industry.
 Able to work in fast-paced environment, provide advice under tight deadlines and competent in managing a varied workload independently.
 A good sense of humor.

Additional Information

We offer a hybrid working pattern of 3 days in the office and 2 days WFH. Our main office is located in the iconic Television Centre (TVC) at White City, London.

We are a Disability Confident Employer and are committed to providing a fair assessment process and are happy to discuss and explore reasonable adjustments during the hiring process. Publicis Groupe UK fosters and inclusive environment through our inspirational Employee Action Groups (EAGs).

Benefits

We have a comprehensive benefits offering. Our full health and lifestyle benefits package will be shared with you, when you join us. In addition to key benefits like Pension, Life Assurance, Income Protection and Private Medical, some of our other benefits are:

Annual Leave (25 days plus 8 bank holidays), increasing after 5 years, by 1 day per additional service up to 30 days. Birthday Day Off that can be used in your birthday month and the opportunity to Buy or Sell Holiday at the start on each year.
Flexible Bank Holidays, you can switch the 2 Easter bank holidays for other days of your choosing. Reflection Days for time away from work to focus on what works best for you. Work your World, after completion of one year, you have the opportunity to work anywhere in the world, where there is a Publicis Groupe office, for up to 6 weeks a year.
Help@Hand, our lifestyle and wellbeing app that supports you and your family; 24/7 Helpline, Remote GPs, Medical or 2nd Opinion, Mental Health & Wellbeing, Physiotherapy, 1-2-1 Lifestyle Coaching, Nutritional Consultations, Savings & Discounts and lots more. 
Inclusive Policies to support you and your family including enhanced Family Leave, Disability, Carers, Transitioning at Work, Flexible Working, Menopause.
Local discounts, restaurants & retailers in Westfield White City. Onsite Café with complimentary breakfast, a subsidised lunch menu, and an in-house barista.

This is an exciting opportunity to influence a global People Technology transformation, helping us navigate an increasingly complex international privacy and AI regulatory landscape. You’ll translate complex legislation into practical, proportionate solutions that enable innovation while protecting our people and our business.

You’ll work across global and regional teams to shape how people data is collected, accessed, stored, processed, transferred and retained throughout the employee and candidate lifecycle.

A key part of the role will be helping Lockton navigate the rapidly developing area of AI and automated decision-making within People Technology.

You’ll be responsible for:

Acting as the privacy and data governance lead across global People Technology transformation initiatives. 
Defining and maintaining our People data governance model, including appropriate access, ownership, sharing, retention and controls.

Monitoring global privacy legislation and translating regulatory change into practical requirements for People, Technology and local teams. 
Ensuring ongoing compliance with UK and EU GDPR and relevant privacy regulation across the jurisdictions in which we operate.

Qualifications

Demonstrable experience leading data privacy in a global, multi-jurisdiction environment, ideally with a focus on people data.

jobs.descriptionText:
About the job
Company Description

We’re a leading Investor Services group offering end-to-end services in administration, accounting, reporting, regulatory and compliance needs of the investment sector worldwide. Our services are underpinned by a Group-wide commitment to ESG and best-in-class technology including a global data platform and innovative proprietary tools supported by in-house experts.

Above all, what makes us different is our people. Operating as trusted partners to our clients, we deliver intelligent solutions through a combination of technical expertise and strong relationships based on deep client understanding. 

We’re driven by our Group purpose, to power people and possibilities.

Job Description

To provide support for all aspects of the development and delivery of the Group’s Data Protection strategy, including to support the operationalisation and management of the Privacy and Data Protection risk management framework.

The role will provide expert technical advice and support to Clusters and to Group support functions.

Working as part of the Group Data Protection Team, the post will also assist the Group DPO to oversee and support the work of the Privacy and Data Protection Analyst(s).

About the job
Job Title

Data Privacy Manager

Job Description

Data Privacy Manager

About IG Group

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here.

About The Role

IG's Data & AI team is scaling up how the business governs, understands, and trusts its data. As our Data Privacy Manager, you'll be the Group's central point of contact for data privacy - closing the gap between policy and practice, taking ownership of the RoPA process, DPIAs, DSAR protocol, retention practices, and breach reporting, and giving IG a single accountable home for data privacy compliance.

About The Team

This role sits within the Data & AI team, reporting into the Head of Data Governance & Strategy. This is an individual contributor role and the first hire into a newly centralised function, so it requires someone comfortable working on their own initiative and building relationships with stakeholders at all levels. As the function scales, this role will pick up direct reports.

Key Responsibilities

As Data Privacy Manager, you'll lead the strategic and day-to-day agenda for data privacy at IG, partnering closely with Legal, Risk, Compliance, HR, Procurement, Technology, and Product colleagues. You'll help evolve a privacy capability that is rigorous where it needs to be and practical everywhere it can be.

Be the central point of contact for data privacy - act as the go-to for all data privacy related questions across the Group, from policy interpretation to practical guidance for staff at all levels. 
Support the governance framework - support the development of the data privacy governance framework, from DPIAs and privacy by design to retention, RoPA and third-party diligence. 
Own cross-border data transfers - put in place and maintain the mechanisms that allow personal data to move lawfully between IG's UK, EU and international entities, such as Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement, and adequacy assessments. 
Own the regulatory interface - manage breach notifications to the relevant regulator within the required regulatory timeframe, DPIA consultations, and centralised data privacy reporting to SLT/Board. 
Advise on privacy by design - advise product and business teams on the privacy implications of new products, changes and customer journeys. 
Translate law into practical guidance - translate UK privacy law into clear, proportionate recommendations that enable responsible decisions. 
Manage complex privacy incidents - including regulatory notification and engagement with affected individuals where required. 
Strengthen privacy awareness - across the business and help build out the privacy function as it grows - running training programmes that go beyond policy awareness to cover breach recognition and escalation for all staff. 
Contribute to the Group's approach to data risk - across a broad range of business activity. 

Role Requirements

5+ years' experience - in a dedicated data privacy role within a regulated environment. 
Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and EU GDPR - together with practical awareness of other privacy regimes relevant to IG's international footprint, including practical experience running DPIAs, RoPA and DSAR processes end-to-end. 
Experience operating within a multi-jurisdictional group structure - (e.g. UK, EU, APAC). 
Experience designing and embedding privacy governance documentation - policies, procedures, and escalation routes, ideally in an organisation without an existing dedicated function. 
Comfortable acting as the primary point of contact - for regulators, and for internal Audit and Risk stakeholders, on data privacy matters. 
Strong communication skills - able to translate legal and regulatory requirements into practical guidance for Product, Technology, HR, and other business teams. 
Experience delivering data privacy training and awareness programmes. 

Desirable

Experience in UK financial services or a similarly regulated industry. 
Practical exposure to AI/ML-related privacy considerations - (e.g. automated decision-making, Article 22). 
Professional certification in data protection/privacy - (e.g. CIPP/E, CIPM, BCS Certificate in Data Protection).

The Perks

It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on. 

Competitive salary
Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
Private medical cover for you and your family
Life insurance
Contribution to gym memberships
25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
The option to buy or sell holiday days
A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents

jobs.descriptionText:
We are looking for an experienced Information Governance Manager to join our Corporate team, reporting to the Company Secretary and General Counsel in their capacity as our statutory Data Protection Officer.This is a part-time role (0.6 FTE) for a specialist who thrives on embedding good information governance across a busy healthcare environment – keeping the organisation compliant, investigating incidents thoroughly, and helping colleagues at every level handle personal and sensitive data with confidence.St John & St Elizabeth Hospital is a leading private hospital in London, offering a comprehensive range of specialist medical treatments, clinics and diagnostic services from a team of world-class consultants, supported by a dedicated team of clinical and non-clinical staff.We are known for our exceptional standards of care, excellent nursing standards, and cutting-edge medical treatments.We have 170 years of history and are looking for people to join us for the next chapter. We are very unique as the only truly charitable private hospital in London and as a charity, every private patient treated helps support our on-site community hospice.Am I the right person for the Information Governance Manager?
You will have substantial experience in information governance or data protection, ideally gained in a hospital or comparable regulated setting, and be confident applying the rules to real, practical situations.
You will hold – or be actively working towards – a recognised data protection or information governance qualification (for example the BCS Practitioner Certificate in Data Protection or IAPP CIPP/E), or be able to demonstrate equivalent professional experience.
You will have a working knowledge of the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the common law duty of confidentiality, along with an awareness of ICO guidance; familiarity with the Caldicott Principles and the NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit would be a real advantage.
You will have a track record of investigating information governance incidents and personal data breaches, handling data subject requests to statutory deadlines, and developing and delivering training that raises awareness across an organisation.
Above all, you will bring sound analytical judgement, discretion and the highest standards of integrity, the ability to influence and challenge colleagues at all levels, and the resilience to work autonomously and prioritise competing statutory deadlines.
What are the responsibilities of the Information Governance Manager?
As the operational lead for information governance, you will support the Data Protection Officer to ensure HJE remains compliant with the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, ICO guidance and sector best practice, including the NHS Data Security and Protection Toolkit.
You will investigate information governance incidents and complaints, working closely with the DPO, SIRO and Caldicott Guardian to assess risk and potential breaches, meet the 72-hour reporting window where required, and turn lessons learned into lasting good practice.
Day to day, you will develop and deliver information governance training and guidance, maintain policies, privacy notices and the IG risk register, and carry out audits and compliance spot checks across the Hospital and Hospice.
You will work with Information Asset Owners to map assets and data flows and maintain the centralised Register of Processing Activities, support colleagues with Data Protection Impact Assessments, and – under the supervision of the General Counsel – review Data Sharing Agreements and carry out supplier due diligence.

jobs.descriptionText:
About the job
At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.

About The Legal, Compliance, And Public Affairs Team

The Legal, Compliance, and Public Affairs team is a group of dedicated professionals committed to helping Affirm scale, innovate, and provide outstanding products for consumers, merchants, and key partners. We combine legal, compliance, and policy expertise to guide growth, shape products, and build trust across our ecosystem. Our work spans multiple professional disciplines and provides the foundation for Affirm’s mission to deliver honest financial products.

About The Role

The Manager, Regulatory Compliance & Privacy (DPO) will support the UK Compliance function by leading and coordinating key second-line regulatory compliance and privacy oversight activities for the UK entity. This role will serve as the operational lead for UK privacy compliance and Data Protection Officer (DPO) responsibilities, while also supporting broader UK regulatory compliance priorities, including vulnerable customers and other key regulatory expectations and programs. The role will partner closely with Legal, Product, Engineering, Operations, Risk, Financial Crimes, and other Compliance stakeholders to ensure a well-governed, scalable, and effective UK compliance framework.

What You’ll Do

As Manager, Regulatory Compliance & Privacy , serve as the primary operational lead for UK privacy compliance matters and act as the designated Data Protection Officer (DPO) for the UK entity, subject to any final organisational and regulatory approvals.

Lead and oversee on existing key UK privacy governance activities, including Data Protection Impact assessments (DPIA’s), oversight, privacy risk assessments, incident and breach governance, data subject rights processes, retention and deletion governance, and regulatory documentation, where required suggest improvements.

Lead the regulatory input of the firm's Management Information (MI) dashboard for Privacy, to include data relating to consumer outcomes and the firm's meeting of Privacy requirements. Ensure ongoing consideration of the metrics and make recommendations for improvement or updates.

Lead the development of the firm's Privacy Compliance Monitoring Programme (CMP) ensuring its suitability is aligned to the risk appetite of the firm, the regulatory landscape and the market within which the firm operates

Support in completion of the firm's Enterprise wide compliance risk assessment and control inventory, including collecting and documenting results, establishing where opportunities exist and work with internal and external partners to deliver.

Translate legal and regulatory requirements into compliance standards, governance routines, oversight expectations, and program requirements for first-line stakeholders.

Support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the UK regulatory compliance framework across key privacy, conduct and consumer protection areas, including vulnerable customers and other core UK regulatory programs.

Provide second-line challenge and oversight of first-line control environments, including review of control design, identification of gaps, escalation of issues, and remediation tracking.

Maintain and enhance governance processes for UK compliance issues management, risk assessments, control oversight,and reporting.

Support internal audit, external audit, regulatory enquiries, and external partner review activity, including coordination of materials, tracking of actions, and remediation governance.

Prepare recurring management reporting, governance materials, and issue summaries for senior leadership and relevant governance forums.

Partner with Legal to ensure clear delineation between legal advisory responsibilities and Compliance operational / oversight responsibilities, particularly in the privacy space.

Partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, and other cross-functional stakeholders to ensure UK privacy and regulatory requirements are operationalised effectively.Coordinate with regional and global Compliance partners to support consistency in governance standards, documentation, and reporting across jurisdictions.

Help identify and implement improvements to compliance processes, governance routines, documentation standards, and oversight tools.

Showcase Compliance as an open for business function, accessible and relatable to the goals and objectives of the firm.

What We Look For

6+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, privacy compliance, risk management, governance, audit, or a related control

function, preferably within financial services, fintech, banking, or another regulated environment, ideally past experience acting as a DPO in a regulated consumer credit firm.

Strong understanding of UK privacy and regulatory compliance expectations, including UK GDPR, governance, DPIA’s, breach

processes, data subject rights, consumer protection, conduct risk, vulnerable customers, and related compliance program requirements.

Experience operating within a second-line of defence model, including governance, oversight, monitoring, and independent challenge of first-line control environments.

Demonstrated ability to translate legal and regulatory requirements into policies, standards, procedures, governance routines and control expectations.

Experience supporting audits, regulatory exams, control reviews, or similar oversight processes in a regulated environment.

Strong cross-functional partnership skills, with the ability to work effectively with Legal, Marketing, Product, Engineering, Operations, Risk, and Compliance stakeholders.

Sound judgment, strong organisational discipline, and the ability to manage sensitive regulatory matters with discretion and rigor.

Experience preparing management reporting, governance materials, and escalation summaries for senior stakeholders.

Ability to manage multiple workstreams and move between strategic governance design and day-to-day execution.

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience; relevant certifications.

Base Pay Grade - L

Equity Grade - 5

Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills.

Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidised medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

GBR base pay range per year: £101,000 - £149,000

Location: Remote UK

Remote-first with flexibility built in

Affirm is proud to be a remote-first company. Most roles can be done from almost anywhere within the country of employment. Some positions may occasionally require in-person work at an Affirm office, and a few are office-based due to the nature of the work. All new hires will be invited to attend an in-person onboarding experience.

Benefits Designed For You

Our benefits reflect our commitment to care, transparency, and flexibility. Here are a few highlights:

Health coverage at no cost: We cover 100% of premiums for employees and their dependents.
Spending stipends: Monthly stipends support your tech setup, and the ability to choose health and wellness options that are right for you.
Time off to recharge: Flexible time off and generous holiday calendars help you rest when you need to.
Own a piece of what you build: Our employee stock purchase plan (ESPP) lets you buy Affirm stock at a discount.

We’re committed to providing an inclusive interview process, including accommodations for candidates with disabilities. If you need support, we’re happy to help.

For positions based in San Francisco or Los Angeles: Affirm considers qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, as required by law.

By clicking "Submit Application," you acknowledge that you have read Affirm's Global Candidate Privacy Notice and consent to the use of your personal information as described.

ntroduction

At Gallagher, we help clients face risk with confidence because we believe that when businesses are protected, they’re free to grow, lead, and innovate. You’ll be backed by our digital ecosystem: a client-centric suite of consulting tools making it easier for you to meet your clients where they want to be met. Advanced data and analytics providing a comprehensive overview of the risk landscape is at your fingertips. Here, you’re not just improving clients' risk profiles, you’re building trust. You’ll find a culture grounded in teamwork, guided by integrity, and fueled by a shared commitment to do the right thing. We value curiosity, celebrate new ideas, and empower you to take ownership of your career while making a meaningful impact for the businesses we serve. If you’re ready to bring your unique perspective to a place where your work truly matters; think of Gallagher.

Overview

Join Gallagher’s Global Privacy Office and play a key role in managing privacy risks across mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures. You’ll help shape the future of privacy within a global organisation that values integrity, collaboration, and innovation. This is your chance to make a real impact in a fast-paced, supportive environment where your expertise will be valued.

How You'll Make An Impact

In this role, you’ll lead data & privacy due diligence for mergers and acquisitions, ensuring risks are identified and managed effectively. You’ll work closely with teams across the business to integrate acquired entities into our privacy framework and support divestitures.

You’ll also help implement Gallagher’s Global Privacy Framework, provide expert advice on data & privacy risks, and deliver training to colleagues. From conducting risk assessments to supporting data subject rights requests, your work will help protect personal and commercial data while enabling business growth.

Key responsibilities include:

Managing data & privacy risks throughout the M&A lifecycle. 
Conducting due diligence and creating integration plans. 
Advising on privacy considerations for transitional service agreements. 
Supporting privacy compliance and incident management. 
Collaborating with teams across Legal, IT, HR, and more. 

About You

You’re a privacy professional with experience in operational or consultative roles. You have a strong understanding of UK and European data protection laws, including GDPR, and experience in M&A due diligence.

You’re a clear communicator who can explain complex privacy issues in simple terms. You’re a team player who thrives in a global, fast-paced environment and is comfortable working with diverse stakeholders.

What we’re looking for:

Privacy certifications (e.g., CIPP/E, CIPM) are a plus. 
Experience conducting privacy risk assessments and transfer impact assessments. 
Strong analytical and interpersonal skills. 
A commitment to integrity and doing business the right way. 
Exposure to OneTrust systems would be advantageous. 

If you’re ready to take the next step in your career and make a difference at a company that champions growth and collaboration, we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation And Benefits

Competitive compensation
Comprehensive benefits programs designed to support your well-being 
Career development opportunities and ongoing learning 
A collaborative, people-first culture with accessible leadership 
The opportunity to do meaningful work with global reach and local impact 

At Gallagher, we are dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to join our Talent Community to stay connected to additional career opportunities. Although this role is listed as full-time, if you’re in a job-share partnership, work reduced hours, or have any other flexible arrangement, please still get in touch. We will also offer reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process if required, so please let us know.

Gallagher is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer (Minorities/Females/Veterans/Disabled)

jobs.title: Head of Data Protection
jobs.descriptionText:
Who are we?

Howden is a collective - a group of talented and passionate people all around the world. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mind-set, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 100 countries. Our people are our biggest asset as well as our largest shareholder group and are everything that makes us unique; our inclusive culture, the quality service we offer our clients, and our continued growth, all come from our people-first approach. There's no such thing as individual success. We all need to play our part, contributing our skills and experience to make a true difference. That's Howden. 

Why work at Howden?

We have always been employee-owned and driven by entrepreneurial spirit. Right from the beginning, we've focused on employing talented individuals and empowering them to make a real difference to the company, whilst building successful and fulfilling careers at the same time. Simply put, we hire talented specialists and give them what they need to make a difference for clients. Always have, always will. People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It's what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down disappointed head-hunters for years. Whatever your priorities - work/life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering - you'll find like-minded people driving change at Howden. 

What is the role?

Head of Data Protection Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance shall lead the Data Protection Function that is responsible for developing, implementing, embedding and maintaining a data protection control and oversight framework for Howden's UK Broking (including its Specialty and Retail Pillars) and UK Reinsurance Divisions. The framework must be pragmatic, risk based and suitably robust to support Howden's UK Broking and UK Reinsurance entities to meet applicable data protection legislation, including the UK Data Protection Act, but also any other applicable legislation in territories where those entities operate. The framework must also align to and complement Howden Group's overarching Data Protection framework, governance and policy. 





What will you be doing?



Oversight & Change

Work closely with Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance senior leadership to develop and drive a data protection strategy that is aligned to the operating model and strategies of those businesses, promoting and supporting consistency of approach and application as much as practically possible. 
Develop and maintain an annual Data Protection Plan setting out the resources needed to deliver the projects and activities to be undertaken by the function, which shall be aligned to and support the regulatory expectations and objectives of the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses (which may include their overseas operations). 
Support in developing and maintaining a data protection risk and control framework, including data protection policy, processes, procedures, controls and monitoring.
Implementing a data protection horizon scanning process, ensuring any new or changing legislation is identified and implemented by expected timeframes.
Produce reports and escalate data protection updates, risks, issues and compliance performance to the relevant Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance governance committees.
Establish and maintain an effective data protection risk identification and escalation process across all Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses, ensuring swift and timely mitigation or management of risks and breaches. 
Develop, maintain and promote the consistent use of data protection tooling.
Continually raise awareness of data protection and ensure adequate programme of data protection related training to employees.
Oversee and manage any reporting to and interaction with data protection supervisory authorities, including the Information Commissioner's Office.
Ensure that all Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses have the correct data protection registrations and licences.
Support in embedding a data protection by design approach within Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses. 
 

Stakeholders



Develop and maintain appropriate working relationships with the following to ensure that data protection issues are identified and proactive provision of appropriate solutions:

Key senior leadership across the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses to ensure a strong understanding of their current and future strategies, business models and objectives, to proactively pre-empt and recognise the data protection support they will require.
Key operational and functional heads that are responsible for the development and delivery of operational processes and systems to embed a data protection by design approach and to support swift escalation of risks and concerns.
Key information security leadership and functions, to ensure a clear understanding of information security processes and controls, and how these dovetail and work alongside data protection controls and risk mitigants.
Internal Control Function Heads across the first, second and third line of defence, to develop an aligned and complementary risk, control and assurance framework, and to support addressing remedial actions.
Group Head of Data Protection and wider group data protection functions to support an alignment of approach, ensure consistent upward escalation and reporting and to share best practice and common risks and issues.  
 





Function responsibilities

To develop, support and maintain a data protection function that is able to achieve the following for Howden's UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses.
Providing timely and considered advice and guidance on a range of data protection matters relating to Howden's UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses, this will include, but will not be limited to - Marketing, DPIA's, Subject Rights, Privacy Notices, Data Security.
Supporting compliance with the UK Data Protection Act, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), other Data Protection Laws and the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR).
Establish processes to monitoring compliance with the EU GDPR and other data protection laws, such as the UK Data Protection Act 2018, our data protection policies, including internal data protection activities, raising awareness of data protection issues, training staff;
Providing advice on the conduct of and supervising data protection impact assessments (DPIAs);
Completing a Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) that cover each of the in scope entities within Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance.
Complete annual Data Protection Risk Assessments for Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance, ensuring that these are reported to the relevant governing committees, but that they also support and contribute to wider Howden Group Data Protection Risk Assessments and ERICCA.
Support in the development and on-going reporting of KRI and KCIs that feed into the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance risk management framework and, where relevant, Howden Group risk management framework and ERICCA. 
Having regard to the risk associated with processing operations and taking account of the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing
Prioritising focus on the more risky activities, e.g. where special category (sensitive) personal data is processed, or where the potential impact on individuals could be damaging;
Establishing clear points of contact for all BAU data protection queries from Howden's UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses with regard to potential complaints and breaches, ensuring that data subject rights' requests accurately handled
Making available data protection resources, policies, procedures, guidance, training material and points of contact information in a way that is easily accessible.
 

Team management

Develop and maintain a function with the appropriate blend of skill, experience and knowledge to deliver the data protection support and oversight required by the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses.
Implement an approach to employee development which enables employees to enhance their data protection, industry and Howden knowledge, experience and skill set.
Provides visionary leadership by fostering a culture of employee engagement and role modelling, encouraging and rewarding essential behaviours and maintaining a high level of personal and professional confidence
Manages (resource, motivate, drive, develop and focus) the team to ensure the required standards of performance are met; and that the professional and personal development of all team members increases their capability and effectiveness
Promotes individual accountability through an ongoing performance management approach that aligns personal performance goals with the functional and wider business goals
Ensures there are effective succession plans in place and actively develops team members to provide future successors
Identifies and hires talent
Manage (resource, motivate, drive, develop and focus) the UK data Protection Function to ensure the required standards of performance are met; and that the professional and personal development of all team members increases their capability and effectiveness
Actively undertakes personal development to ensure up to date knowledge and understanding of best practice
Develop and maintain appropriate working relationships with the following to ensure that data protection issues are identified and proactive provision of appropriate solutions:
Key senior leadership across the Howden UK Broking and UK Reinsurance businesses to ensure a strong understanding of their current and future strategies, business models and objectives, to proactively pre-empt and recognise the data protection support they will require.
Key operational and functional heads that are responsible for the development and delivery of operational processes and systems to embed a data protection by design approach and to support swift escalation of risks and concerns.
Key information security leadership and functions, to ensure a clear understanding of information security processes and controls, and how these dovetail and work alongside data protection controls and risk mitigants.
Internal Control Function Heads across the first, second and third line of defence, to develop an aligned and complementary risk, control and assurance framework, and to support addressing remedial actions.
Group Head of Data Protection and wider group data protection functions to support an alignment of approach, ensure consistent upward escalation and reporting and to share best practice and common risks and issues. 





What are we looking for?

Ability to provide risk-based advice.
Experience in achieving stated objectives involving a diverse set of business partners and leading multifaceted projects.
Negotiation skills to work effectively with key internal and external partners.
Client relationship skills to continuously coordinate with controllers and processors while maintaining independence.
Interpersonal skills to communicate well with a wide-ranging audience, from the Board of Directors to data subjects, from managers to IT staff and lawyers.
Self-starter with ability to gain required knowledge in wide-ranging environments.
Experienced within a Data Protection compliance field, to include building, implementing and managing data protection programmes within a sophisticated and enterprise-wide organisation.
Experience with supporting marketing initiatives and the PECR regulations.
Experience in handling data subject rights requests.
Detailed knowledge of UK and European data protection law, and an in-depth knowledge of the GDPR.
An understanding of technical and operational measures that should be in place to ensure the security of personal data and familiarity with information technologies and data security.
Experience in compliance monitoring and risk management.
Experienced in producing and presenting data protection reports to senior governance committees.
Experienced in developing and delivering data protection training to employees of all levels.
Financial Services experience preferred.
 

Compliance & Regulatory Responsibilities

Compliance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), UK Data Protection Act 2018, other UK data protection / privacy related legislation (such as the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations) and ICO guidance related to the tasks of a DPO.
 

Professional Qualifications

CIPP/E or Certified Data Protection Practitioner (PC.dp) preferred but not essential
 

What do we offer in return?

A career that you define. Our business succeeds by allowing our people to make a mark in the areas they care about most: personal development, volunteering, and fundraising for charity, or creating new insurance products that address society's greatest challenges.And we know that separate home and work lives don't really exist. If you're happy and healthy at home, you're more likely to be happy and fulfilled at work - and vice versa. That's why we do our best to support our people in every aspect of their lives.Diversity and Inclusion At Howden we value diversity - there is no one Howden 'personality type'. Instead, we're looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
We support each other, in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
We are determined to make a positive difference, at work and beyond
We consider our people our chief competitive advantage and as such we treat colleagues, candidates, clients, and business partners with equality, fairness, and respect - regardless of age, disability, race, religion or belief, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, or family circumstances. 

Our sustainability promise

We're on a life-long journey to become an ever-more sustainable group. It's a commitment to taking care of our people and the world we live in, to doing good business, and to making a positive impact wherever we can. Our governance processes, company policies, and review systems are all geared towards our goal of making a positive impact in the world. You can read more about our sustainability work here.
Desired Skills and Experience

Data Protection
Privacy
GDPR

Engage meaningfully in the culture of the General Counsel’s Organization

Operate consistent with principles of stewardship, operating effectiveness and leadership excellence

To be successful in this role you will have...

Expertise with the General Data Protection Regulation, EU AI Act, as well as other global privacy laws, regulations, and industry guidelines, especially those relevant for the asset management industry in EMEA and APAC

The ability to analyse legislative requirements and relate these to organisational practices and solutions

Ability to effectively operate and partner as part of a global team, but with individual accountability on a day-to-day basis

Demonstrated strong analytical skills, including the ability to assess risk and impact from a privacy and data protection perspective

Experience managing complex projects, including prioritizing and working alongside cross-functional, global teams

Highly professional with ability to handle confidential information, remain impartial and influence people at all levels internally and externally

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to adapt to different audiences and leadership styles

An innovative mindset with the ability to work on own initiative with minimal supervision

Ability to juggle conflicting demands and effectively prioritise

Aptitude for and interest in learning evolving technology

Continuous improvement mindset

If you also had this, it would be great...

Previous experience in a similar role within the asset management industry

CIPP/E Certification (highly desirable)

In-Office Collaboration

We are a client-centric, relationship-based business. Working together, in-person, is foundational to how we achieve results. ***Applications read by a human.***

 

Are you a OneTrust expert who loves to work in a team and knows how to solve problems?  We see you!

 

Why should this job matter for you?

 

We give you a platform to connect with global brands to solve challenges that few can.

 

If you are interested in carving out your space to help global players govern their AI programmes, understand evolving privacy regulations or implementing risk controls, we might be the right fit for you.

 

If you live in the London area, you will be based 2 days in our London office and the rest from home. If you don’t, but you think you would be a great asset to our team, we would be happy to have you work fully remotely.

There may be some occasional travel required.

We offer 26 days of annual leave, in addition to UK bank holidays, pension contributions and a work-from-anywhere policy for 6 weeks each year.




Our clients are in a constant search for experts in this field and consultants they can trust. This is how we build meaningful partnerships with our clients, so we are on the constant lookout for colleagues to learn from.

 

In this role, you will

 * Lead data privacy engagements end to end, from scoping through delivery
 * Run the data protection function on behalf of clients, including DPO support delivered as a service
 * Advise senior stakeholders on GDPR, cross border transfers, and the harder regulatory judgement calls
 * Oversee OneTrust configuration and use within the privacy programmes you lead

In practice, that means owning the running of a privacy function for the clients who look to us to hold that responsibility on their behalf. You will advise at board level, triage what matters from what does not, handle the regulator facing conversations when they arise, and bring the technology, the people, and the regulation together into a programme that actually works.

You will contribute to how we work. Our privacy practice is growing, and the people who join at this level will help shape how we deliver DPO support, how we scale across clients, and how we take the service to the market.

 

Must haves

 * Hands on experience configuring or implementing OneTrust
 * Experience with some of these modules: Privacy Management, Consent and Preference, Third Party Risk, AI Governance or Data Discovery
 * Deep expertise in Data Protection, AI Governance and/or Governance, Risk and Compliance
 * A right to work in the UK

 

We hope you…

 * Have a positive mindset
 * Are driven and a self-starter
 * Know a second language
 * Worked in consulting before, whether at a professional services firm, a Big Four, or a privacy specialist firm
 * Have learned from past challenges and can think creatively out of challenges
 * Are familiar with adjacent privacy and GRC platforms (TrustArc, Securiti, BigID, ServiceNow GRC, or similar)




The rest can be learnt within our team.

 

Our Mission

We connect clients to tailored compliance solutions within privacy, AI governance, GRC.

When regulators add more requirements to privacy, AI and data landscapes, clients come to our door to address these challenges. That’s our business. Solving compliance requirements before they become issues.

Apply to learn how you can showcase your experience on a global scale.

Your next journey starts here.

Remote (UK-based)

About Us

Reachdesk is the first truly end-to-end global SaaS gifting and swag platform, helping B2B companies create meaningful connections with prospects, customers, and employees, while driving measurable ROI.

We believe gifting is more than just a transaction: it’s about building genuine human connections that fuel business growth. Whether you’re engaging prospects, celebrating customers, or recognizing employees, our platform makes it easy to deliver personalized gifts, branded swag, and unforgettable event & brand experiences at scale through automated sourcing, storage, and global delivery.

We’re growing, and we’re currently looking for a Head of Business Systems & Security to join us.

The Role

As Head of Business Systems & Security you will own the platforms Reachdesk runs on, the security programme our customers rely on, and the IT that keeps the company working. That covers NetSuite, Salesforce, Workato and DealHub among others, the integration layer and data definitions beneath them, SOC 2 and access control, and the full device and application estate across our UK, US and Portugal teams. It is a broad, senior remit with real autonomy: you will decide how we use our systems, not simply keep them running.

This is a rare opportunity to shape a systems function rather than inherit one. You will set the architecture, governance and roadmap, lead a small team of engineers alongside specialist delivery partners, and work directly with the executive team and with every part of the business that runs on these systems. Beyond the estate itself, you will carry a standing mandate to find the manual work across the business, automate it, and make every other team measurably faster. This department is also our AI enabler: you will decide how Reachdesk adopts AI, and make it part of how people actually work rather than something they experiment with.

Responsibilities


 * Own the business systems estate end to end: NetSuite, Salesforce, Workato and DealHub among them, the integrations that connect them, and the data governance underneath.
 * Set the architecture, operating model and roadmap for how Reachdesk uses its systems.
 * Own the SOC 2 Type II programme, the security policy set and the risk register as the accountable business owner.
 * Own identity and access management, joiner, mover and leaver processes, and the device and endpoint estate across three countries.
 * Lead customer security assurance, from questionnaires and RFPs through to enterprise due diligence.
 * Own the tech stack and application estate, including licence and spend decisions, consolidation and renewals.
 * Own how Reachdesk adopts AI: the tools we invest in, the workflows we rebuild around them, and the training that keeps people using them well.
 * Run our AI governance framework, covering acceptable use, data handling and the controls our customers and auditors expect.
 * Take a standing remit to go into other teams’ processes, automate what should not be manual, and publish the impact.
 * Lead and grow a small team of systems engineers, and manage specialist delivery partners including our Salesforce implementation partner.
   
   

About You


 * 5+ years in business systems, IT or BizTech leadership within B2B SaaS, including at least 3 years leading a function or team, ideally in a PE-backed environment.
 * Deep, hands-on ownership of an enterprise CRM, ERP and the integration layer between them. We run Salesforce, NetSuite and Workato; equivalent platforms translate.
 * Accountable ownership of a SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 programme, rather than supplying evidence into someone else’s.
 * Identity and access, SSO and device estate ownership at a hundred-plus headcount across multiple countries.
 * Still hands-on in the systems themselves, and able to walk through what you have configured, built or designed in detail rather than at a summary level.
 * Genuinely strong with AI: you use it daily in your own work, you can tell a real use case from a demo, and you have put it into workflows other people depend on.
 * The technical judgment to say whether an approach is the right one, and the confidence to tell a senior stakeholder when the process is the problem rather than the tooling.
 * Able to translate technical trade-offs into commercial impact for any audience, from the executive team to the people who use the systems every day.
 * Pragmatic about buying versus building, unsentimental about tools, and drawn to a broad remit with a small team rather than the reverse.
   
   

The Benefits


 * Competitive salary with generous stock options
 * Pension with employer contributions (NEST)
 * Affordable Private Medical Insurance, including mental health support and fast access to care
 * Flexible PTO that increases the longer you’re with us, plus extra flexibility for life’s unexpected moments
 * A genuinely collaborative culture with innovative, fun, and ambitious people
